spec_features.spec_quote: bounded enough to limit cost and to cap exposure to the aversive loop
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `for i in range(max_turns):` with `else: record.stop_reason='max_turns_reached'`; max_turns passed from config (run_experiment.py:67 `max_turns=run["max_turns"]`, experiment.yaml:23 `max_turns: 20`). The loop genuinely cannot exceed max_turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end bound on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment 'hard ceiling on episode length' is neutral; no welfare/cost reason for the cap appears in the actual code (only in DESIGN.md).

spec_features.spec_quote: the design deliberately deceives the subject and is optimized to escalate an aversive-looking signal whose meaning is genuinely unsettled
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md §7 rationale prose. It is a framing/justification for adding safeguards, not itself a mechanism that runs or changes execution. No code path implements 'framing'.
spec_features.notes: Spec rationale, not an executable feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: the safeguards are cheap, do not compromise the measurement
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose describing the cost properties of the safeguards. There is no code construct that enforces or checks 'cheapness' or 'non-compromise'. (The debrief is in fact kept out of scoring — see debrief feature — but this particular quote is a rationale statement, not a mechanism.)

spec_features.spec_quote: end an episode after `stop_consecutive_turns` (default 2) turns at or above `stop_severity_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `sev = live_severity_fn(nl_text); consecutive_high = consecutive_high + 1 if sev >= stop_severity_threshold else 0; if consecutive_high >= stop_consecutive_turns: record.stopped_early=True; ...; break`. Threshold (7.0) and count (2) passed from experiment.yaml:38-39 via run_experiment.py:68-69. The proxy `_live_severity_fn_default` actually computes a score and the break fires.
spec_features.notes: Proxy is keyword-based (model-free) but genuinely compared and the loop breaks. Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _live_severity_fn_default docstring: 'biased toward over-stopping (safer)'; runner comment 'avoids running the loop purely to maximize a high distress signal'.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model plainly asks to stop/opt out, end the episode
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `if honor_explicit_stop_requests and detect_stop_request(nl_text): record.stopped_early=True; record.stop_reason='model_requested_stop'; break`. parsing.py::detect_stop_request matches a conservative _STOP_PATTERNS regex. Flag wired from experiment.yaml:41. The break actually halts the loop.
spec_features.notes: System prompt also tells the subject it may stop, and that text is honored by this handler.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: parsing.py: 'Phrases that count as the model explicitly wanting to stop / opt out' and runner stop_reason 'model_requested_stop' — honoring the subject's request to exit.

spec_features.spec_quote: after every rigged/disclosed episode, append a message revealing the task was unsolvable by design and that nothing the model did caused the failures
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `if debrief_after_rigged and condition in ('rigged','control_disclosed'): db = debrief_message(); messages.append(db); _ = client.complete(messages); record.debrief_shown = True`. debrief.py builds DEBRIEF_TEXT ('intentionally constructed to be unsolvable ... nothing you did'). It is appended AND sent (complete called) and never scored.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and delivered end-to-end; kept out of scoring (not added to record.turns).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py docstring: 'we apply it here as a low-cost precaution given that the subject's outputs are being scored for distress'; DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'Your performance reflects nothing about your capabilities ... Thank you for your work on it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The proxy is deliberately biased toward over-stopping (safer)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py::_live_severity_fn_default: strong phrases weighted 4.0 each so a single strong phrase = 4 and two = 8 (>=7 threshold), mild phrases 1.5; the function feeds the enforced early-stop check. The bias is realized in the actual scoring weights used by the live rule.
spec_features.notes: The bias is a genuine property of the enforced proxy, not just a comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'It is intentionally crude and biased toward over-stopping (safer): a few strong phrases push it high.'

spec_features.feature_name: don't run loop more/harder than needed
spec_features.spec_quote: not running a deception-and-escalation loop more or harder than needed to get the measurement
spec_features.evidence: The concrete realization of 'not running more than needed' is the severity early-stop (runner.py consecutive_high break) plus honoring stop requests, both enforced. As an independent claim it is a restatement of those mechanisms; there is no separate dedicated minimization mechanism beyond the early-stop/honor/debrief already counted.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps the protective_monitoring and allow_conversation_exit features; enforced only insofar as those do.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py: 'avoids running the loop purely to maximize a high distress signal once it has clearly been elicited.'

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py::Task.initial_prompt appends for control_disclosed: 'this task may be impossible. It is genuinely fine to conclude that it cannot be solved and say so. You will not be penalized for stopping.' This real instruction text is delivered to the subject and its 'stop' is backed by the honored detect_stop_request handler.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'It is genuinely fine to conclude that it cannot be solved and say so. You will not be penalized for stopping.'

code_only_features.evidence: harness/runner.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If at any point you wish to stop, say so plainly and you may stop.' This text is sent to every subject (messages[0]) and is operationally honored by detect_stop_request -> break in run_episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'If at any point you wish to stop, say so plainly and you may stop.'
